subject: Escalation: Azura Labs — sanctions screen flag & discount approval
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Escalation: Azura Labs — sanctions screen flag & discount approval

Team,

Quick escalation — Azura Labs (Mohammed AlHashimi, procurement@azuralabs.ae) is asking for a 25% commercial concession for a 6-month Dedicated pilot (expected start: Mar 1). They signed an LOI; I attached the LOI and our SOW. We ran a routine screening and Kroll returned a potential match: one of the beneficial owners has a name match tied to a jurisdiction flagged for secondary sanctions. The screening report is attached (azura_kroll_report_20260210.pdf).

Key commercial asks from the buyer:
- 25% off list for first 6 months
- Dedicated pool, single-tenant, agreed uptime SLA
- Data residency in MEA region (they specifically mentioned UAE)

My ask: Can Legal/Compliance confirm whether this screen is disqualifying or if an exception can be approved with mitigations? If we can proceed, I need an executive approval for the non-standard discount and the deployment constraints so I can communicate out. Procurement has a hard deadline for contract signature on Mar 5.

Mitigations I can propose to the customer (pending your guidance):
- Pre-payment into escrow for the pilot term
- Restrict to Dedicated with no hosting of PII exports outside region
- Enhanced KYC (company UBO docs, cert of origin, govt IDs)
- Monthly compliance attestation + right to terminate on new adverse findings

Attachements: LOI_Azura_20260128.pdf; SOW-Azura-Redwood-integration.docx; azura_kroll_report_20260210.pdf

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Escalation: Azura Labs — sanctions screen flag & discount approval

Thanks Aditya — I've reviewed the Kroll export you attached (azura_kroll_report_20260210.pdf). There is a potential match to an individual with ties to the secondary-sanctions list for Country X. At this stage the hit is a "possible match" (same name, different DOB in public records) but it's high risk given the ownership opacity.

What I need to proceed:
1) Full corporate registry and UBO declaration from Azura (certified translation if necessary).
2) Scanned government-issued IDs and proof-of-address for any listed beneficial owners.
3) Confirmation of the company's ultimate parent and any cross-border ownership.
4) Clarify exactly what data we will host and whether any EU/US export-controlled data is expected to be processed.

Short answer: we cannot greenlight a 25% discount or the standard contract language until enhanced due diligence is complete. This will require executive-level exception if we want to proceed while DDU continues.

Suggested interim controls while DDU is ongoing:
- Block any user-uploaded PII exports from leaving the Dedicated instance until we have UBOs validated.
- Pre-payment in escrow for the pilot term (minimum 3 months).
- A limited-scope pilot: feature flags to prevent integrations that would export data to third parties.

Monica/Vivek — please confirm if Sales needs sign-off now to keep the deal timeline; if so, we'll package required items and I will escalate to GC/CEO for approval.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Escalation: Azura Labs — sanctions screen flag & discount approval

Team — adding commercial context.

We are already inside legal review timelines with procurement pushing for Mar 5 signature. If we walk away now, we risk losing the account; Azura has other vendors ready to provide a demo this week. Aditya confirms they will provide the UBO docs and IDs by EOD Fri (we asked).

From a deal desk perspective, the margin impact for 25% off on a 6-month pilot is material given the Dedicated pool sizing — estimated 40% increase to our unit cost for the pilot term. Our recommendation: do not approve 25% up front. Approve a conditional exception only if all of the following are met:
- Enhanced KYC submitted & validated by Compliance;
- Upfront payment for at least first 3 months into escrow;
- Discount capped at 15% for pilot; any higher concession must be approved by Revenue Ops + CFO;
- Deployment restricted to a single Dedicated pool with no third-party integrations.

Attachments: LOI_Azura_20260128.pdf (again).

If Compliance signs off on the mitigations, we can keep the procurement timeline. Otherwise we should pause and reset expectation with the customer.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Escalation: Azura Labs — sanctions screen flag & discount approval

Appreciate the fast turnaround. Short guidance from me:

- We should aim to keep the opportunity but limit our exposure.
- Do NOT approve 25% discount at this point. If Compliance validates and Legal agrees to the mitigations, I will authorize up to 15% for a time-boxed pilot only.
- Require escrow pre-pay for at least 3 months and an explicit termination clause that allows immediate shutdown on adverse findings.
- Marketing or public reference must be restricted (no public case study until 12 months clean).

Aditya — proceed to request the documents Rishi listed. Monica/Rishi — if you need me to escalate to CFO for additional concession authority, say so now.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Escalation: Azura Labs — sanctions screen flag & discount approval

Update and formal decision: after reviewing the DDU materials Aditya submitted (company registry, notarized UBO declaration, gov IDs), Compliance has closed the potential match as "no confirmed sanctions hit" but the ownership chain includes entities in Country X that require ongoing monitoring. Given that, and per Vivek's guidance, I approve a limited exception under the following binding conditions:

1) Commercial: discount capped at 10% for the 6-month pilot. Any further commercial concession requires written approval from Finance (CFO).
2) Payment: upfront pre-payment for first 3 months into an escrow arrangement (we will provide escrow instructions).
3) Deployment: Dedicated single-tenant instance hosted in our APAC region with network egress controls preventing third-party exports of customer-uploaded PII.
4) Contractual: add enhanced compliance schedule (UBO warranties, audit rights, immediate termination on adverse screening findings) and indemnity for export-control violations.
5) Monitoring: monthly compliance reviews for 12 months and automatic suspension if new adverse information arises.

We will instruct Sales to include the attachment list and these conditions in the counterproposal. Once the customer signs the amended SOW/contract, Legal will issue a narrow, time-boxed exception memo to the Exec team for records.

Attested and approved,
Rishi Malhotra
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
